subject: City Council Candidate Forum
overview: The Medford Democratic City Committee hosted a public forum for the fourteen candidates running for Medford City Council. Each candidate delivered a five-minute statement regarding their policy priorities, qualifications, and vision for the city's future.

items.title: Forum Introduction and Rules
items.summary: Moderators welcomed the public and established the five-minute time limit for each candidate following a lottery for speaking order.

items.title: Candidate Adam Knight
items.summary: The incumbent focused on public safety accomplishments, including funding for a new police station and fire headquarters, alongside infrastructure and school improvements.

items.title: Candidate Natalie Breen
items.summary: The first-time candidate emphasized the need for a young female voice on the council and advocated for better utilization of city assets like the Mystic River and historic buildings.

items.title: Candidate Ann Marie Cugno
items.summary: The School Committee member discussed her record of local and state advocacy while calling for the immediate implementation of the city's master plan for Medford Square.

items.title: Candidate Curtis Tuden
items.summary: The candidate centered his platform on environmental sustainability, proposing community energy aggregation and sanctuary city status for Medford.

items.title: Candidate Michael Marks
items.summary: The incumbent highlighted his efforts regarding pedestrian safety, charter review, and the development of the city's first dog park.

items.title: Candidate Breanna Lungo-Koehn
items.summary: The incumbent advocated for transparency in government, a nationwide search for a new school superintendent, and simultaneous renovations for police and fire facilities.

items.title: Candidate Fred Dello Russo
items.summary: The incumbent spoke on the importance of collaborative relationships in government to achieve long-term goals like the new library and police station projects.

items.title: Candidate Robert Cappucci
items.summary: The candidate proposed establishing municipal term limits, ending paid parking in city squares to support local businesses, and taking a 'tough love' approach to the opioid crisis.

items.title: Candidate George Rick Sacco
items.summary: The candidate called for a dedicated budget line item for opioid response and urged a formal review of the 30-year-old city charter.

items.title: Candidate John Falco
items.summary: The incumbent noted his initiatives to improve government transparency through legislative software and his advocacy for hiring a municipal traffic engineer.

items.title: Candidate Ray Scarfo
items.summary: The candidate criticized the existing city charter for concentrating power in the mayor's office and questioned current water and sewer tax policies.

items.title: Candidate George Scarpelli
items.summary: The incumbent highlighted the creation of a full-time recreation department and expansion of vocational programs at the high school during his term.

items.title: Candidate Richard Caraviello
items.summary: The Council President discussed securing a library grant and his efforts to maintain critical care services at Lawrence Memorial Hospital.

items.title: Candidate Cheryl Rodriguez
items.summary: The candidate proposed high-end commercial development for Mystic Avenue and zoning reforms that require residential developers to fund affordable housing.
